what: A devnet probe: may a FlopSessionKeys session call the ComputeChannel pallet?
answer: Yes, as far as the session's pallet filter goes. A session whose allowed pallets are [ComputeChannel] passed ComputeChannel.timeout through to the ComputeChannel pallet (it failed there with ChannelNotFound, as it must for a made up channel id). The same session refused System.remark with PalletNotAllowed. So ComputeChannel is not on the session pallet's deny list, and the allow list takes the metadata's pallet name.
not_shown: That open_channel or top_up_escrow succeed through a session, how the session's spend meter counts the escrow they move, and what the hosted gateway does. No channel was opened and no inference was bought.

owner.role: the agent's FLOP identity; it created the session

device.role: a new key made for this probe (wallets/flop-probe-device.key); the session's delegate

steps.note: 0.1 FLOP moved from the owner to the new device account, so the device can pay its own fees

steps.what: FlopSessionKeys.create_session: let 0x1ec8abdfa88707679f8a2fbfc0bcd80184e2f731d91bb9fa152b750210556c7f spend from the signer's account, lifetime cap 100000000000000000 raw (0.1 FLOP), per call 50000000000000000 raw (0.05 FLOP), per day 100000000000000000 raw (0.1 FLOP), for 7200 blocks, allowed pallets ComputeChannel
steps.note: FlopSessionKeys.SessionCreated: lifetime cap 0.1 FLOP, per call 0.05 FLOP, per day 0.1 FLOP, expires at block 3499918, allowed pallets ComputeChannel

steps.what: FlopSessionKeys.execute_via_session: as owner 0xe462d014cab1239a123233647052f4e3b572322e982441d6b7a5c1694d8419e2, declared spend 0 raw (0 FLOP), session nonce 0, run: ComputeChannel.timeout on channel 0x696d642d666c6f702d73657373696f6e2d70726f62652d32303236313131312e
steps.result: ExtrinsicFailed: Module error, pallet 103 error 7 = ComputeChannel.ChannelNotFound
steps.note: the session let the call through and the ComputeChannel pallet answered. The channel id is made up, so no channel was touched. After it the session nonce is still 0 and the session and breaker counters are unchanged: the whole call was rolled back. The device still paid the fee.

steps.what: FlopSessionKeys.execute_via_session: as owner 0xe462d014cab1239a123233647052f4e3b572322e982441d6b7a5c1694d8419e2, declared spend 0 raw (0 FLOP), session nonce 0, run: System.remark "imd-flop session probe"
steps.result: ExtrinsicFailed: Module error, pallet 94 error 7 = FlopSessionKeys.PalletNotAllowed
steps.note: the control: a call to a pallet that is not on the session's list is refused by the session pallet itself

steps.what: FlopSessionKeys.revoke_session: end the session of delegate 0x1ec8abdfa88707679f8a2fbfc0bcd80184e2f731d91bb9fa152b750210556c7f
steps.note: FlopSessionKeys.SessionRevoked. The session record stays in storage with active false. DelegateSessions of the device is empty.

steps.what: Balances.transfer_all: send everything the signer has to 0xe462d014cab1239a123233647052f4e3b572322e982441d6b7a5c1694d8419e2 (keep_alive false)
steps.note: the device sent everything it had left back to the owner (83177797660000000 raw). The device account no longer exists on chain.

left_on_chain: Sessions(owner, device) holds the revoked session (active false, nothing spent, expiry 3499918). CircuitBreakers(device) holds an empty record. The owner's account nonce is 3.
how: Each call was built and signed offline by tools/flop-session-probe/flop-sign.mjs in the desktop shell (the keys stay on the PC), checked with TaggedTransactionQueue_validate_transaction, sent with author_submitAndWatchExtrinsic through the browser, and read back from System.Events at the finalized block. Calls and storage keys were checked against the polkadot-api reference encoder first. Events were decoded with the polkadot-api reference decoder and our recorded metadata.
